hook_text: Long ago, a message could take months to arrive. Today, you can send one around the world in less than a second.
clip_script: Firelight in a cave long ago: a storyteller speaks while others listen. A San artist paints an eland on a rock wall. A runner races across the veld with a message. Then a letter in an envelope, a telegraph clicking, a black telephone ringing, a radio crackling, a TV flickering, and finally a cell phone buzzing with a video call from another continent. Ways to share a message have changed again and again, but people still love to talk and tell stories.
visual_style: Whiteboard timeline: a speech bubble, a rock painting, a drum, a scroll, a letter, a telephone, a radio, a TV and a smartphone, with a line underneath reading still talking face to face.
mood: Warm and curious, like a family gathering full of stories.
pacing: Quick jumps through history, then slow down on what has stayed the same.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and ask an older person how they sent messages when they were young.
